calls.reason: The statement is explicitly hedged. Microsoft's filing reports construction commitments, but no separate CIP balance that establishes the $50 billion estimate.
Meta and Alphabet report higher depreciation, but litigation, taxes and investment losses complicate profit comparisons. These results do not settle the undated prediction of broad profit erosion.
Alphabet describes supply constraints, while Microsoft reports faster GPU deployment and added capacity. Neither establishes whether deployment difficulties extend across the industry.

CoreWeave's reported 500 MW addition challenges the negligible-capacity premise, but power alone does not establish usable compute. The packet does not establish whether slow supply creates illusory demand.
The Yahoo Finance report gives Microsoft's AI power capacity, not GPU inventory values or installation costs. It cannot establish either of the claimed dollar amounts.
Meta's Q2 remarks document earlier depreciation pressure at one company. They do not settle the forecast of a future hyperscaler depreciation spike or establish the treatment of the relevant GPUs.
